source_metadata.title: Empagliflozin monotherapy with sitagliptin as an active comparator in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial
source_metadata.source_type: multicentre randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3 trial

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial evaluated the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of empagliflozin monotherapy compared with placebo and sitagliptin in previously untreated adults with type 2 diabetes, with a separate open-label empagliflozin 25 mg cohort for HbA1c above 10%.
The randomized cohort included 899 participants: 228 assigned placebo, 224 empagliflozin 10 mg, 224 empagliflozin 25 mg, and 223 sitagliptin 100 mg.

population.label: Randomized HbA1c 7.0% to 10.0% cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: The open-label cohort included 87 participants with screening HbA1c above 10% assigned empagliflozin 25 mg for 24 weeks.

population.label: Open-label HbA1c greater than 10.0% cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: Randomized-treatment eligibility required no oral or injected anti-diabetes treatment during the preceding 12 weeks and screening HbA1c of 7.0% to 10.0%, except the German range was 7.0% to 9.0%.

population.label: Randomized-treatment candidates
inclusion_criteria: No oral or injected anti-diabetes treatment for 12 weeks before randomization
HbA1c 7.0% to 10.0% at screening, or 7.0% to 9.0% in Germany

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants had to be adults, with the country-specific age rules of at least 20 years in Japan and 18 to 65 years in India, and BMI no greater than 45 kg/m2.

population.label: Trial candidates
inclusion_criteria: Adult age threshold with country-specific rules

atoms.canonical_statement: Key exclusions included confirmed fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L during run-in, eGFR below 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 or below 60 in China, contraindications to sitagliptin, recent antiobesity treatment, systemic steroids, recent thyroid-hormone dose changes, or another uncontrolled endocrine disorder.

population.label: Trial candidates
exclusion_criteria: Confirmed fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L during run-in
eGFR below 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 or below 60 in China
Uncontrolled endocrine disorder other than type 2 diabetes

atoms.canonical_statement: Empagliflozin 10 mg was administered orally once daily for 24 weeks in the randomized triple-dummy trial.
Empagliflozin 25 mg was administered orally once daily for 24 weeks in the randomized triple-dummy trial; the same dose was used open-label for the HbA1c-above-10% cohort.
Sitagliptin 100 mg once daily for 24 weeks was the active comparator, and placebo was the control, within a triple-dummy randomized design.
The primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline in HbA1c at week 24.
Key secondary efficacy endpoints were change from baseline in bodyweight and change from baseline in systolic and diastolic blood pressure at week 24.

concept.text: Change from baseline in bodyweight and blood pressure

atoms.canonical_statement: Exploratory efficacy endpoints included HbA1c below 7% at week 24, fasting plasma glucose, greater than 5% bodyweight reduction, waist circumference, and blood-pressure control below 130/80 mm Hg.

concept.text: Exploratory glycemic, weight, waist, and blood-pressure outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety assessment included adverse events, serious and severe adverse events, confirmed hypoglycemia, events consistent with urinary tract infection, and events consistent with genital infection.

concept.text: Adverse events and prespecified safety events

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial enrolled participants at 124 sites in nine countries and used a 2-week open-label placebo run-in before randomized treatment.
Eligible randomized participants were allocated 1:1:1:1 with a computer-generated sequence in blocks of four, stratified by region, screening HbA1c category, and screening eGFR category.
Patients, investigators, and individuals involved in trial-data analysis were masked to randomized treatment assignment; the randomized phase used a triple-dummy design.

Rescue glucose-lowering medication was permitted for fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L during weeks 1 to 12 or above 11.1 mmol/L during weeks 12 to 24; GLP-1 agonists and DPP-4 inhibitors were not permitted as rescue.
The primary ANCOVA included treatment, region, and baseline eGFR category as fixed effects and baseline HbA1c as a covariate in the full analysis set.
Post-rescue efficacy values were treated as missing and missing week-24 values in the primary ANCOVA were imputed with last observation carried forward.

The study used a hierarchical confirmatory testing procedure with a two-sided 2.5% significance level for each empagliflozin dose to control familywise error across the primary and key secondary endpoints.
Sensitivity analyses included mixed-model repeated-measures analyses using observed cases and per-protocol ANCOVA analyses.
The trial was registered as NCT01177813.
At week 24, empagliflozin 10 mg reduced HbA1c by an adjusted 0.74 percentage points more than placebo.

Overall, 803 of 899 randomized participants completed 24 weeks of randomized treatment.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study was sponsored by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly.
Boehringer Ingelheim participated in study design, data collection, and analysis; Eli Lilly co-sponsored the study but did not participate in study design, data collection, or analysis.
Jens Eilbracht, Bruno Delafont, Gabriel Kim, Hans J Woerle, and Uli C Broedl were employees of Boehringer Ingelheim.

Michael Roden reported advisory-board or speaker relationships with Takeda, Eli Lilly, and Novo Nordisk, consulting for Sanofi-Aventis, and clinical-trial involvement with Novartis and Boehringer Ingelheim.
Jianping Weng reported research support from Eli Lilly, Bayer, and Novo Nordisk.
The 24-week treatment period does not establish long-term durability of glycemic, weight, blood-pressure, or safety effects.
Because metformin was already recommended as first-line therapy in most settings, a drug-naive placebo-controlled monotherapy comparison had limited direct alignment with usual treatment pathways.
Comparisons between empagliflozin and sitagliptin were exploratory, so the study was not designed to support definitive comparative-efficacy conclusions between those active treatments.
The HbA1c-above-10% cohort received open-label empagliflozin 25 mg without randomized placebo or sitagliptin comparison, limiting causal interpretation for that cohort.
The trial assessed surrogate metabolic and hemodynamic outcomes over 24 weeks and did not test cardiovascular, kidney, hospitalization, or mortality outcomes.
The authors concluded that empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg monotherapy improved glycemic control and reduced bodyweight and systolic blood pressure in previously untreated type 2 diabetes.
The authors considered empagliflozin generally well tolerated over 24 weeks, with confirmed hypoglycemia similar to placebo and genital infections more frequent with empagliflozin.
